_comment: Proposed by rigor workstream A6 (numerical verification). The main agent merges these into experiments/queue.json AFTER the 7-hour campaign. Nothing here has run on a GPU.

items.title: SQ150: GPU numerical suite for the fla kernels (gpu_numerical_suite.py): behavioural API contract, kernel vs fp64 over a T x d grid (fp32/bf16, chunk/recurrent/neg-eig), backward vs fp64 autograd, long-T (8k, 16k) chunked vs streamed vs prefill+decode, real GatedDeltaNet block and whole model vs the fp64 reference, attention/SWA/MLP/BitLinear on GPU vs fp64
items.why: The audit's C2 'textbook example': a kernel was declared broken because of a call-site bug. This item re-validates every kernel contract and confirms (or recalibrates) the CPU-derived mixed-precision budgets (C198). The CPU emulation under-predicts the fp32 chunk kernel's error by 2.8-3.5x; this run measures the real budget utilisation per cell.

launch.precondition: experiments/staged-tests/ moved to tests/ (or run in place), GPU slot free, no GPU process (bash experiments/launch/status.sh), no campaign item running
launch.after: python experiments/staged-tests/run_numerical_suite.py --gpu --stamp   # records the GPU pass in env_fingerprint.json

items.title: SQ153: why is the fp32 chunk kernel 3x less accurate than a TF32-dot emulation? (input_precision / dtype of intermediates), <= 3 GPU-min
items.why: Recorded GPU error of chunk_gated_delta_rule in fp32 is 2.2e-4 (SQ70) vs 7e-5 predicted by rounding every matmul operand to TF32; bf16 and the recurrent kernel are within 0.7-1.3x. If an intermediate is stored in bf16, 'fp32' runs are not fp32 at all, which matters for any fp32-vs-bf16 comparison.
missing: script (read fla/ops/gated_delta_rule/chunk*.py for tl.dot input_precision and intermediate dtypes; run with each candidate emulation); needs SQ150's per-cell numbers
